title: Investigation of Metabolic Processes during Caloric Restriction and Subsequent Surplus
summary: Overweight and obesity are increasing worldwide, raising the risk for various diseases, such as diabetes and cardiovascular conditions. Long-term weight loss can help reduce this risk. However, many people who initially succeed in losing weight regain the lost weight or even exceed their initial body weight. During the subsequent weight gain, there is a disproportionate increase in fat mass. The exact metabolic processes that explain the preferred increase in fat mass are still unclear. Therefore, the aim of the study is to investigate the metabolic processes responsible for the excessive increase in fat tissue after caloric restriction.

interventions.name:
Caloric Deficit Followed by a Caloric Surplus:
Study participants go through 3 days in energy balance, 3 days in an energy deficit (50% of their energy requirement), followed by 3 days in an energy surplus (150% of their energy requirement).

Caloric Surplus Followed by a Caloric Deficit (Control):
Study participants go through 3 days in energy balance, 3 days in a caloric surplus (150% of their energy requirement), followed by 3 days of caloric restriction (50% of their energy requirement).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Age between 18 and 35 years
-Body Mass Index (BMI) between 18.5 and 25 kg/m²
-No history of disturbed eating behavior or eating disorders
-No diagnosed metabolic diseases (e.g., no hypothyroidism, no diabetes mellitus)
-No repeated major weight losses in the past
-Weight fluctuations of ≤2.5 kg in the last 3 months
-No vegan diet
-No nutrient intolerance or food allergies
-Women: Regular periods in the last three months (cycle length >35 days), no use of a hormonal IUD, not pregnant, and not breastfeeding
Exclusion criteria:
-Age <18 or >35 years
-Body mass index <18.5 or >25 kg/m²
-History of disturbed eating behavior/eating disorders
-Diagnosed metabolic disease (e.g. hypothyroidism, diabetes mellitus)
-Repeated major weight loss in the past
-Weight fluctuations of >2.5 kg in the last 3 months
-Vegan diet
-Nutrient intolerance or food allergy
-Women: no regular period in the last three months (cycle length >35 days), use of a hormonal IUD, pregnancy, or breastfeeding
